analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: Torah #42 (LM2) consists of exactly two lines. Line 1 cites the verse 'כִּי אֲנִי יְיָ רֹפְאֶךָ' (Exodus 15:26) and notes that the roshei-teivot (initial letters) form the words 'אָמֵן כֵּן יְהִי רָצוֹן'. Line 2 is a parenthetical: 'וְעַיֵּן בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּאוּר עִנְיָן זֶה' — see elsewhere for the explanation of this matter. The Torah contains no bechina language ('הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', etc.), no conceptual equivalences, no thematic development, and no named concepts that could be assigned to packages. The acronym observation is a purely structural/mnemonic relationship, not a bechina (shared-nature) or eitza (cause-effect) relationship. There are no missing bechina nodes to flag because the text introduces no bechina claims.
